[USER] When we write the scientific name of an organism we have to write it in:  
[USER] Group of answer choices: italics, CAPITALS, bold, Greek  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] When writing the scientific name of an organism, it should be written in italics.  
[USER] The Kingdom ______ includes organisms ranging from green algae to flowering plants.  
[USER] Group of answer choices: Animalea, Fungi, Protista, Plantae  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The Kingdom "Plantae" includes organisms ranging from green algae to flowering plants.  
[USER] Which of these plants is named for its shape?  
[USER] Group of answer choices: poison oak, cattails, Gerber daisy, fever few  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Cattails are named for their shape. The cylindrical brown spikes on the plant resemble the tail of a cat, hence the name cattails.  
[USER] Which term comes next: kingdom, phylum, class, ______....  
[USER] Group of answer choices: order, genus, family, species  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The term that comes next after kingdom, phylum, and class is "order". The taxonomic hierarchy goes as follows: kingdom, phylum, class, order, family, genus, species.  
[USER] In the list of taxonomy classification, related family are grouped into which category?  
[USER] Group of answer choices: species, class, order, phylum  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Related families are grouped into the category of "order" in taxonomy classification. The taxonomic hierarchy goes as follows: kingdom, phylum, class, order, family, genus, species.  
[USER] Guam disease has been attributed to the toxins found in which of the following groups?  
[USER] Group of answer choices: ferns, pine trees, cycads, palm trees  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Guam disease has been attributed to the toxins found in "cycads". Cycads are a group of plants that are known to produce toxins, including the neurotoxin BMAA (beta-methylamino-L-alanine), which has been linked to the development of Guam disease.  
[USER] Carolus Linnaeus named the plants according to number, arrangement and length of:  
[USER] Group of answer choices: sepals, petals, stamen, carpels  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Carolus Linnaeus named plants according to the number, arrangement, and length of "stamens and carpels". This system of classification is known as the sexual system, where plants were classified based on their reproductive organs.
